description: The Path-Merging Sieve detects when the trajectory of n joins the trajectory of a smaller number n_1, even if T^k(n) has not yet descended below n. If T^k(n) is congruent to 2 mod 3 and (2*T^k(n) - 1)/3 < n, then n's path merges with a previously-verified path. Analogous to common subexpression elimination in compilers.
mathematical_formalization: If m = T^k(n) and m is congruent to 2 mod 3, then m = T((2m-1)/3). If (2m-1)/3 < n, convergence of (2m-1)/3 implies convergence of n. Detection: m mod 3 depends only on last k bits of n.
implementation_hypothesis: Track m mod 3 using Lemma 2.8 (count even steps after last odd step) instead of explicit division. Implement as a 2-bit counter: reset on odd steps, increment on even steps. Path merging applies when counter is even and (2m-1)/3 < n.
experiment_seed: Measure additional pruning rate beyond Descent Sieve alone for N=40..60. Compare mod-3 counter vs explicit modular arithmetic cost.
